text:
{
  "claims": [
    {
      "anchor": "SQLite normally keeps the WAL file in check by automatically checkpointing it at the end of any transaction once it exceeds 1000 pages",
      "claim_text": "In its default configuration, SQLite checkpoints the WAL file at the conclusion of any transaction when the WAL file is more than 1000 pages long.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P3.S1", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P3.S1."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "transferring its contents into the main database file",
      "claim_text": "Checkpointing transfers WAL contents into the main database file.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P1.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "the entire WAL has been transferred into the database"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "P1.S0 describes WAL transferred into the database."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "rewinding the WAL so new transactions start at the beginning",
      "claim_text": "Checkpointing rewinds the WAL so new transactions start at the beginning.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P1.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "rewind the WAL back to the beginning and start putting new transactions at the beginning of the WAL"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "P1.S0 states the rewind behavior."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "if the application disables or defers the automatic checkpoint mechanism through compile-time or run-time options, nothing prevents the WAL from expanding indefinitely",
      "claim_text": "If an application disables the automatic checkpoint, nothing prevents the WAL file from growing excessively.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P3.S3", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P3.S3."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "compile-time or run-time options",
      "claim_text": "Compile-time and run-time options exist that can disable or defer the automatic checkpoint.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P3.S2", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P3.S2."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "a checkpoint can only run to completion and reset the WAL when no other connections are using it",
      "claim_text": "A checkpoint is only able to run to completion and reset the WAL file if there are no other database connections using the WAL file.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S1", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P4.S1."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "a database with many concurrent overlapping readers and at least one always-active reader will never let a checkpoint finish",
      "claim_text": "If a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P5.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P5.S0."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "it cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction",
      "claim_text": "The WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S1", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P7.S1."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "a big change to a big database can produce a very large file until the transaction commits",
      "claim_text": "A large change to a large database might result in a large WAL file until the write transaction completes.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S2", "rel": "entails"}, {"sid": "P7.S3", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "P7.S2 and P7.S3 together state this."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "on SQLite versions before 3.11.0, a transaction that grows larger than the page cache could write the same page into the WAL multiple times",
      "claim_text": "With older versions of SQLite, the same page might be written into the WAL file multiple times if the transaction grows larger than the page cache.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P8.S2", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": {"kind": "version", "left": "3.11.0", "op": "<", "right": "3.11.0"},
      "reasoning": "P8.S2 states this for older versions; version check confirms 'before 3.11.0'."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "applications should leave automatic checkpointing enabled",
      "claim_text": "Applications should leave automatic checkpointing enabled.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": false,
      "evidence": [],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passages describe disabling as a cause of growth but do not explicitly recommend leaving it enabled."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "keep read transactions short",
      "claim_text": "Applications should keep read transactions short.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": false,
      "evidence": [],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passages mention reader gaps but do not recommend short read transactions."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "ensure there are \"reader gaps\"—times when no processes are reading from the database—so checkpoints can complete",
      "claim_text": "This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are reader gaps: times when no processes are reading from the database and checkpoints are attempted during those times.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P6.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P6.S0."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "running manual checkpoints with the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART or SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE option guarantees the checkpoint runs to completion before returning",
      "claim_text": "Running manual checkpoints with SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART or SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE ensures that the checkpoint runs to completion before returning.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P6.S1", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P6.S1."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "TRUNCATE also shrinks the file to zero",
      "claim_text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE shrinks the WAL file to zero.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": false,
      "evidence": [],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passages do not state that TRUNCATE shrinks the file to zero."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "the tradeoff is that readers may block while it runs",
      "claim_text": "The disadvantage of using SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE is that readers might block while the checkpoint is running.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P6.S2", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Direct restatement of P6.S2."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "upgrading to SQLite 3.11.0 or later ensures a single transaction's WAL footprint is proportional to the transaction itself",
      "claim_text": "As of SQLite version 3.11.0, the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size to the transaction itself.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": true,
      "evidence": [{"sid": "P8.S0", "rel": "entails"}],
      "check": {"kind": "version", "left": "3.11.0", "op": ">=", "right": "3.11.0"},
      "reasoning": "P8.S0 states this as of 3.11.0."
    },
    {
      "anchor": "pragmas like wal_autocheckpoint and journal_size_limit can be used to tune the checkpoint threshold and cap the file's size on disk",
      "claim_text": "Pragmas like wal_autocheckpoint and journal_size_limit can be used to tune the checkpoint threshold and cap the file's size on disk.",
      "kind": "direct",
      "sure": false,
      "evidence": [],
      "check": null,
      "reasoning": "Passages do not mention these pragmas."
    }
  ]
}
